# UniGL Spoofer A Zygisk module that changes the GPU (OpenGL ES / Vulkan) and device info an app sees, so games can offer graphics settings that are normally limited to specific devices. Works with any Zygisk. Android 8.0+, arm64-v8a and x86_64.

## Install 1. Flash the zip in your root manager and reboot. 2. Open the module's WebUI (KernelSU, KernelSU-Next, APatch, or WebUI-X on Magisk). 3. Add the app's package name, choose a profile, force stop the app, and start it again. The app must not be on a denylist or unmount list, otherwise Zygisk skips it. Settings are stored in `/data/adb/unigl/` (`targets.conf` and `profiles/*.conf`). ## Profiles Every profile comes in two flavors: - **Minimal**: GPU strings (OpenGL ES renderer and vendor, Vulkan device name), manufacturer, and model. Start here. - **Full**: Minimal plus Vulkan vendor ID, brand, board, hardware, and SoC model/manufacturer. Built-in profiles follow the top of the AnTuTu Android ranking (October 2026, global): | # | Device | Model | GPU | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | HONOR Magic9 Pro Max | WKL-AN20 | Adreno 850 | | 2 | RedMagic 11 Pro | NX809J | Adreno 840 | | 3 | POCO F9 Ultra | 26077PC53G | Adreno 840 | | 4 | iQOO 15 | I2501 | Adreno 840 | | 5 | OnePlus 15 | CPH2747 | Adreno 840 | | 6 | Xiaomi 17 Ultra | 2512BPNDAG | Adreno 840 | | 7 | POCO F8 Ultra | 25102PCBEG | Adreno 840 | | 8 | OPPO Find X9 Ultra | CPH2841 | Adreno 840 | | 9 | Samsung S26 Ultra | SM-S948B | Adreno 840 | Some model numbers come from pre-release listings, so double-check them if you can. Adreno 840 profiles are the safest first choice since newer GPUs may not be recognized by every app. Built-in profiles cannot be edited or deleted. Create your own under **Custom profiles** in the WebUI. Every key is optional, and an empty value leaves the real value untouched. **Profile specs** shows what any profile changes. ## What it changes | Target | Method | |---|---| | `glGetString` (vendor, renderer, version, extra extensions) | GOT hook on `glGetString`, `eglGetProcAddress`, `dlsym` | | Vulkan device name, vendor ID, device ID, driver version | hook on `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(2/2KHR)` and `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` | | `android.os.Build` fields | JNI static fields | | `ro.product.*`, `ro.hardware`, `ro.board.platform`, `ro.soc.*` | hook on `__system_property_get` | ## Limitations - Only the app's own libraries are patched, not system libraries. - 64-bit only. - Libraries that use packed relocations (`DT_ANDROID_RELA`) are not hooked. - CPU cores, RAM, and refresh rate are not changed. - Server-side checks cannot be bypassed. - Spoofing device info in online games may violate their terms of service. ## Uninstall - **One app:** tap **Remove** next to it in the WebUI and force stop the app. No reboot needed. - **Everything:** disable or remove the module in your root manager and reboot. To delete the settings too, run `su -c "rm -rf /data/adb/unigl"`. - **App crashes and the WebUI is not reachable:** run `su -c "rm /data/adb/unigl/targets.conf"` and reboot, or create `/data/adb/modules/unigl_spoofer/disable`. Only listed apps are affected, so this cannot cause a boot loop. ## License MIT. `src/zygisk.hpp` follows the public Zygisk API v4 (0BSD, John Wu). ## Author Amon, Telegram: [@xhamon](https://t.me/xhamon)
readmeHTML:
UniGL Spoofer

A Zygisk module that changes the GPU (OpenGL ES / Vulkan) and device info an app sees, so games can offer

graphics settings that are normally limited to specific devices. Works with any Zygisk. Android 8.0+, arm64-v8a and x86_64.

Install

  • Flash the zip in your root manager and reboot.
  • Open the module's WebUI (KernelSU, KernelSU-Next, APatch, or WebUI-X on Magisk).
  • Add the app's package name, choose a profile, force stop the app, and start it again.

    • The app must not be on a denylist or unmount list, otherwise Zygisk skips it.

    Settings are stored in /data/adb/unigl/ (targets.conf and profiles/*.conf).

    Profiles

    Every profile comes in two flavors:

  • **Minimal**: GPU strings (OpenGL ES renderer and vendor, Vulkan device name), manufacturer, and model. Start here.
  • **Full**: Minimal plus Vulkan vendor ID, brand, board, hardware, and SoC model/manufacturer.

    • Built-in profiles follow the top of the AnTuTu Android ranking (October 2026, global):

    | # | Device | Model | GPU |

    |---|---|---|---|

    | 1 | HONOR Magic9 Pro Max | WKL-AN20 | Adreno 850 |

    | 2 | RedMagic 11 Pro | NX809J | Adreno 840 |

    | 3 | POCO F9 Ultra | 26077PC53G | Adreno 840 |

    | 4 | iQOO 15 | I2501 | Adreno 840 |

    | 5 | OnePlus 15 | CPH2747 | Adreno 840 |

    | 6 | Xiaomi 17 Ultra | 2512BPNDAG | Adreno 840 |

    | 7 | POCO F8 Ultra | 25102PCBEG | Adreno 840 |

    | 8 | OPPO Find X9 Ultra | CPH2841 | Adreno 840 |

    | 9 | Samsung S26 Ultra | SM-S948B | Adreno 840 |

    Some model numbers come from pre-release listings, so double-check them if you can.

    Adreno 840 profiles are the safest first choice since newer GPUs may not be recognized by every app.

    Built-in profiles cannot be edited or deleted. Create your own under Custom profiles in the WebUI.

    Every key is optional, and an empty value leaves the real value untouched. Profile specs shows what any profile changes.

    What it changes

    | Target | Method |

    |---|---|

    | glGetString (vendor, renderer, version, extra extensions) | GOT hook on glGetString, eglGetProcAddress, dlsym |

    | Vulkan device name, vendor ID, device ID, driver version | hook on vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(2/2KHR) and vkGetInstanceProcAddr |

    | android.os.Build fields | JNI static fields |

    | ro.product.*, ro.hardware, ro.board.platform, ro.soc.* | hook on __system_property_get |

    Limitations

  • Only the app's own libraries are patched, not system libraries.
  • 64-bit only.
  • Libraries that use packed relocations (`DT_ANDROID_RELA`) are not hooked.
  • CPU cores, RAM, and refresh rate are not changed.
  • Server-side checks cannot be bypassed.
  • Spoofing device info in online games may violate their terms of service.

    • Uninstall

  • **One app:** tap **Remove** next to it in the WebUI and force stop the app. No reboot needed.
  • **Everything:** disable or remove the module in your root manager and reboot. To delete the settings too, run `su -c "rm -rf /data/adb/unigl"`.
  • **App crashes and the WebUI is not reachable:** run `su -c "rm /data/adb/unigl/targets.conf"` and reboot,

    • or create /data/adb/modules/unigl_spoofer/disable. Only listed apps are affected, so this cannot cause a boot loop.

    License

    MIT. src/zygisk.hpp follows the public Zygisk API v4 (0BSD, John Wu).

    Author

    Amon, Telegram: @xhamon
